title: Self-assembly emerges from cells sharing a common model of organismal form

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Self-assembly emerges from cells sharing a common model of organismal form

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In simulations based on variational free-energy minimization (active inference), cells that share a common genetically and epigenetically specified model of the organism's form self-assemble into that form, offering a proof of principle that self-assembly can be an emergent property of such cells.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Here, we offer a proof of principle that self-assembly is an emergent property of cells that share a common (genetic and epigenetic) model of organismal form.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Friston K, Levin M, Sengupta B, Pezzulo G, “Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation”, Journal of the Royal Society, Interface (2015), doi:10.1098/rsif.2014.1383; section “Abstract”. Scope: Active-inference simulation of eight cells forming a head–body–tail morphology

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-place-01: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.90

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a concrete simulation result and the paper specifies the equations, parameters, and public integration software well enough for reimplementation. The stated conclusion concerns sufficiency in this model, so rerunning it directly discriminates success from failure.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reimplement the eight-cell generative model and test whether identical cells converge from the stated initial condition to the encoded head-body-tail arrangement while ensemble variational free energy decreases. Failure across the stated parameterization would refute the proof-of-principle result.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: The model is a deliberately small proof of principle rather than a calibrated biological model.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.9
data existence: 0.85
operationalizability: 0.95
data adequacy: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is about a stated simulation, and the paper points to a public SPM routine that still implements shared-model self-assembly. Re-running it can confirm or refute that outcome. The default target in the current file has drifted from the 2015 head–body–tail illustration, so the eight-cell case needs the published target mask rather than the file's present bitmap.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run the public active-inference morphogenesis routine from a shared generative model and undifferentiated initial state, and score whether cells migrate and differentiate into the target pattern while ensemble free energy falls. Failure to assemble under that shared model would refute the reported proof of principle.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
MATLAB is required to run the solver as distributed.

The current public script defaults to 16 cells and a target mask that is not the paper's eight-cell head–body–tail figure.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.78
operationalizability: 0.86
analysis feasibility: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.7
data existence: 0.9

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In the paper's eight-cell active-inference model, cells that start identical, co-located and undifferentiated, and that share one generative model of the target form, end a 32-step free-energy descent near the target head-body-tail configuration with the correct cell types, while ensemble free energy falls.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: over 20 random seeds (initial expectations drawn with log precision -4, as in the paper), in at least 16 runs (80%) after 32 time steps (a) the RMS distance between final cell positions and target positions under the best one-to-one assignment is below 0.5 x the smallest distance between two target positions, and (b) at least 7 of 8 cells have their most probable identity (softmax of hidden states) belonging to the cell type encoded at their assigned target location; and in every passing run ensemble free energy at step 32 is below its value at step 1.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: fewer than 10 of 20 runs (50%) meet (a) and (b), or ensemble free energy at step 32 is not below step 1 in the majority of runs. Between 10 and 15 passing runs is pre-registered as 'mixed'.
